1 --- 2 title: Ensuring instant navigations 3 description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations. 4 nav_title: Instant navigation 5 related: 6 title: Learn more 7 description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation. 8 links: 9 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant 10 - app/guides/runtime-prefetching 11 - app/getting-started/caching 12 - app/getting-started/revalidating 13 - app/guides/prefetching 14 --- 15 16 This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests. 17 18 ## What "instant" means 19 20 A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks. 21 22 > **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. 23 24 A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. 25 26 Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout. 27 28
29 Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI 30 31 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. 32 33 On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. 34 35 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load. 36 37
38 39 Runtime prefetching extends the static shell with a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) by invoking the route at prefetch time. Ensuring navigations are instant is the foundation: a route that doesn't navigate instantly without runtime prefetching won't navigate instantly with it either. See [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) for the patterns. 40 41 ## The tools 42 43 ### Build the static shell 44 45 With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell. 46 47 > **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the runtime prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching. 48 49 **``** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves. 50 51 > **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `` boundary further up the tree is needed. With [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), the information is available and such a fallback becomes part of the instant UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback. 52 53 Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route: a fallback that renders instantly during client navigations when nothing else is ready. [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) builds on it, resolving a link's URL data on top. 54 55 ### Tune what `` prefetches 56 57 Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. The shell is shared across every link to the same route, so rendering a `` is effectively free. 58 59 To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch): 60 61 ```tsx 62 63 Checkout 64 65 ``` 66 67 With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click. 68 69 ### Validate instant navigation 70 71 By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached. 72 73 To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`: 74 75 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7} 76 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 77 78 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 79 cacheComponents: true, 80 experimental: { 81 instantInsights: { 82 validationLevel: 'manual-warning', 83 }, 84 }, 85 } 86 87 export default nextConfig 88 ``` 89 90
91 How validation simulates different navigations 92 93 For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 94 95 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 96 97 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 98 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 99 100 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 101 102
103 104 ### Test it in CI 105 106 The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. See [Prevent regressions with e2e tests](#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for the pattern. 107 108 ### Inspect loading states 109 110 The **Navigation Inspector** in the Next.js DevTools freezes the page at its initial loading state, showing the static shell on direct visits and the prefetched destination on client navigations. Use the inspector to see how much meaningful content lands in the shell. 111 112 Pair it with the React DevTools Suspense panel to see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. See [Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) for the workflow. 113 114 See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell) for patterns to reduce fallback coverage and pull more content into the shell. 115 116 ## A page that navigates instantly 117 118 To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The dev overlay doesn't include this in its fix cards because it has bigger implications than the recommended approaches, which keep the page in the server-component model. Reach for `"use client"` when the page is fully interactive and must be a client component. 201 202 > **Good to know**: `"use client"` doesn't skip validation for the static shell. Hooks like `useSearchParams()` still need a `` boundary. 203 204 ## Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools 205 206 As you develop a route, the Next.js DevTools let you see what your users see on page loads and client navigations before dynamic data streams in. Use it to verify that your loading states look right, confirm the content you expect appears immediately, and iterate on where to place `` boundaries. 207 208 The [React DevTools Suspense panel](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) complements this: it lists the `` boundaries in the tree and lets you toggle each one between its fallback and resolved state, so you can see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. 209 210 {/* TODO: screenshot — React DevTools Suspense panel listing boundaries with toggle controls */} 211 212 The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled: 213 214 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4} 215 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 216 217 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 218 cacheComponents: true, 219 } 220 221 export default nextConfig 222 ``` 223 224 Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then toggle **Pause on navigations**. The panel shows **Awaiting navigation...** With the toggle on, the next refresh or link click freezes the page so you can inspect the shell. 225 226 Refresh the product page. The Inspector freezes and shows **Loading shell** labeled **Page load** with the target URL. In the app, two fallbacks appear: "Loading product..." and "Checking availability...". On the first visit the cache is cold and both are visible. 227 228

The Inspector shows **Loading shell** labeled **Client nav** with both source and target URLs. In the app, the product name and price appear immediately (cached). "Checking availability..." shows where inventory will stream in. 251 252

271 272 Toggle **Pause on navigations** off when you're done inspecting loading states. Each navigation pauses as long as the toggle is on. 273 274 > **Good to know:** Page loads and client navigations can produce different shells. Client-side hooks like `useSearchParams` suspend on page loads (search params are not known at build time) but resolve synchronously on client navigations (the router already has the params). 275 276 ## Prevent regressions with e2e tests 277 278 Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship. 279 280 The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`: 281 282 ```bash package="pnpm" 283 pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 284 ``` 285 286 ```bash package="npm" 287 npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 288 ``` 289 290 ```bash package="yarn" 291 yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 292 ``` 293 294 ```bash package="bun" 295 bun add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 296 ``` 297 298 A route can be reached two ways, and a `` boundary can cover one without covering the other: 299 300 - **Initial page load**: Use `page.goto()` to test the static UI from the document response. 301 - **Client navigation**: Click a `` to test the destination's prefetched UI. [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) can add request-specific content to this UI. 302 303 ```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts" highlight={6-14,20-25} 304 import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test' 305 import { instant } from '@next/playwright' 306 307 test.describe('Product page (/store/[slug])', () => { 308 test('is instant on an initial page load', async ({ page, baseURL }) => { 309 await instant( 310 page, 311 async () => { 312 await page.goto('/store/hats') 313 await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap') 314 await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0) 315 }, 316 { baseURL } 317 ) 318 await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible() 319 }) 320 321 test('is instant on a client navigation', async ({ page }) => { 322 await page.goto('/store/shoes') 323 await instant(page, async () => { 324 await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]') 325 await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/store/hats') 326 await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap') 327 await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0) 328 }) 329 await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible() 330 }) 331 }) 332 ``` 333 334 Pass Playwright's `baseURL` to `instant()` when `page.goto()` is the first navigation. The helper needs the origin before requesting the document. 335 336 Inside the callback, an initial page load shows the static UI and a client navigation shows the destination's prefetched UI. Other dynamic content remains blocked until the callback finishes. 337 338 > **Good to know:** The start of the `instant()` scope is the same as turning on **Pause on navigations** in the Navigation Inspector, and the end of the scope releases the pause the way **Resume** does. 339 340 For client navigations, wait for the destination URL before asserting on its UI. Otherwise, a shared selector can match the source page before the destination commits. If the prefetched destination cannot commit, the URL wait times out and the test fails. 341 342 Run these against `next dev`, where the testing API is enabled automatically. To run them in CI against a production build, set `exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild` so `next start` exposes the same API: 343 344 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} 345 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 346 347 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 348 cacheComponents: true, 349 experimental: { exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild: true }, 350 } 351 352 export default nextConfig 353 ``` 354 355 Focus these tests on the user flows that matter most. 356 357 ## Fixing a navigation that blocks 358 359 Consider a different route, `/products/[slug]`, that fetches product data from a public API and shows a featured list alongside: 360 361 ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" 362 export default async function ProductPage( 363 props: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'> 364 ) { 365 const featured = await getFeatured() 366 const { slug } = await props.params 367 const res = await fetch(`https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products/${slug}`) 368 const product = await res.json() 369 370 return ( 371

Both will surface as Instant validation errors, one at a time. 387 388 ### Step 1: Move the slug-dependent work into Suspense 389 390 Validation surfaces the per-slug product fetch first. 391 392

464 465 Add a `"use cache"` directive to the fetching function: 466 467 ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" 468 async function getFeatured() { 469 'use cache' 470 const res = await fetch('https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products?limit=3') 471 return res.json() 472 } 473 ``` 474 475 The result is cached at the fetch level. The featured list ships with the App Shell. 476 477 > **Good to know:** In serverless deployments, in-memory caching with `"use cache"` will not persist across instances. Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching. 478 479 Validation passes. Open the DevTools and try a client navigation. The featured section appears immediately, and **"Loading product..."** shows where the product details will stream in. 480 481 ### Iterate on loading states 482 483 {/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */} 484 485 Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation. 486 487 The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time. 488 489 Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent. 490 491 ## AI workflow 492 493 An AI coding agent can run this workflow to make a navigation instant: 494 495 - **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately. 496 - **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route. 497 - **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or ``). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation. 498 - **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard. 499 500 The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `` rather than guessing a cache lifetime. 501 502 For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down. 503 504 Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers: 505 506 - **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell. 507 - **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile. 508 - **Runtime prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it. 509 510 Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect. 511 512 For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup. 513 514 The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both. 515 516 ## Opting out 517 518 Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes. 519 520 The dev overlay surfaces this as the **Block** fix alongside every insight: 521 522 523 532 533 534 Set `instant = false` on the page or layout file. This opts the segment out of validation feedback. The segment may still navigate instantly if its structure supports it; the framework just won't surface insights for it. Navigations between sibling segments below are still validated. 535 536 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 537 export const instant = false 538 ``` 539 540 With `false` on `/dashboard/layout.tsx`, validation no longer flags navigations into `/dashboard` from outside; navigations between `/dashboard/a` and `/dashboard/b` are still checked. 541 542 For opted-out segments, the navigation blocks on the server. If the content depends on cookies or headers but has a known cache lifetime, caching it with [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) lets the App Shell carry it ahead of the click instead of opting out, as long as its [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time is at least 5 minutes. 543 544 ## Next steps 545 546 - [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the recommended `` defaults and the migration path off `unstable_eager` 547 - [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for the full configuration 548 - [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) when parts of your route depend on URL data (`searchParams` or `params`) and you want it in the shell 549 - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering 550 - [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for how to expire cached data with `cacheLife` and `updateTag` 551

The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the runtime prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching. 48 49 **``** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves. 50 51 > **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `` boundary further up the tree is needed. With [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), the information is available and such a fallback becomes part of the instant UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback. 52 53 Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route: a fallback that renders instantly during client navigations when nothing else is ready. [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) builds on it, resolving a link's URL data on top. 54 55 ### Tune what `` prefetches 56 57 Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. The shell is shared across every link to the same route, so rendering a `` is effectively free. 58 59 To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch): 60 61 ```tsx 62 63 Checkout 64 65 ``` 66 67 With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click. 68 69 ### Validate instant navigation 70 71 By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached. 72 73 To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`: 74 75 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7} 76 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 77 78 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 79 cacheComponents: true, 80 experimental: { 81 instantInsights: { 82 validationLevel: 'manual-warning', 83 }, 84 }, 85 } 86 87 export default nextConfig 88 ``` 89 90

The root layout `` catches everything. 98 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 99 100 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 101 102
103 104 ### Test it in CI 105 106 The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. See [Prevent regressions with e2e tests](#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for the pattern. 107 108 ### Inspect loading states 109 110 The **Navigation Inspector** in the Next.js DevTools freezes the page at its initial loading state, showing the static shell on direct visits and the prefetched destination on client navigations. Use the inspector to see how much meaningful content lands in the shell. 111 112 Pair it with the React DevTools Suspense panel to see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. Each navigation pauses as long as the toggle is on. 273 274 > **Good to know:** Page loads and client navigations can produce different shells. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship. 279 280 The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. If the prefetched destination cannot commit, the URL wait times out and the test fails. 341 342 Run these against `next dev`, where the testing API is enabled automatically. To run them in CI against a production build, set `exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild` so `next start` exposes the same API: 343 344 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} 345 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 346 347 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 348 cacheComponents: true, 349 experimental: { exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild: true }, 350 } 351 352 export default nextConfig 353 ``` 354 355 Focus these tests on the user flows that matter most. 356 357 ## Fixing a navigation that blocks 358 359 Consider a different route, `/products/[slug]`, that fetches product data from a public API and shows a featured list alongside: 360 361 ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" 362 export default async function ProductPage( 363 props: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'> 364 ) { 365 const featured = await getFeatured() 366 const { slug } = await props.params 367 const res = await fetch(`https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products/${slug}`) 368 const product = await res.json() 369 370 return ( 371

Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching. 478 479 Validation passes. Open the DevTools and try a client navigation. The featured section appears immediately, and **"Loading product..."** shows where the product details will stream in. 480 481 ### Iterate on loading states 482 483 {/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */} 484 485 Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation. 486 487 The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time. 488 489 Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent. 490 491 ## AI workflow 492 493 An AI coding agent can run this workflow to make a navigation instant: 494 495 - **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately. 496 - **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route. 497 - **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or ``). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation. 498 - **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard. 499 500 The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `` rather than guessing a cache lifetime. 501 502 For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down. 503 504 Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers: 505 506 - **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell. 507 - **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile. 508 - **Runtime prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it. 509 510 Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect. 511 512 For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup. 513 514 The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both. 515 516 ## Opting out 517 518 Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes. 519 520 The dev overlay surfaces this as the **Block** fix alongside every insight: 521 522 523 532 533 534 Set `instant = false` on the page or layout file. This opts the segment out of validation feedback. The segment may still navigate instantly if its structure supports it; the framework just won't surface insights for it. Navigations between sibling segments below are still validated. 535 536 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 537 export const instant = false 538 ``` 539 540 With `false` on `/dashboard/layout.tsx`, validation no longer flags navigations into `/dashboard` from outside; navigations between `/dashboard/a` and `/dashboard/b` are still checked. 541 542 For opted-out segments, the navigation blocks on the server. If the content depends on cookies or headers but has a known cache lifetime, caching it with [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) lets the App Shell carry it ahead of the click instead of opting out, as long as its [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time is at least 5 minutes. 543 544 ## Next steps 545 546 - [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the recommended `` defaults and the migration path off `unstable_eager` 547 - [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for the full configuration 548 - [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) when parts of your route depend on URL data (`searchParams` or `params`) and you want it in the shell 549 - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering 550 - [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for how to expire cached data with `cacheLife` and `updateTag` 551

1 --- 2 title: instant 3 description: API reference for the instant route segment config. 4 related: 5 title: Next Steps 6 description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice. 7 links: 8 - app/guides/instant-navigation 9 - app/getting-started/caching 10 - app/getting-started/revalidating 11 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache 12 --- 13 14 The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI. 15 16 Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant. 17 18 When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough. 19 20 > **Good to know**: 21 > 22 > - The `instant` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. 23 > - `instant` cannot be used in Client Components. It will throw an error. 24 > - Next.js does not perform prefetches in development, so navigations may not feel as instant as they will in production. Validation reflects what will happen during `next start`, where prefetching is enabled. 25 26 ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher 27 export const instant = true 28 29 export default function Page() { 30 return
...
31 } 32 ``` 33 34 ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher 35 export const instant = true 36 37 export default function Page() { 38 return
...
39 } 40 ``` 41 42 ## Reference 43 44 The export accepts: 45 46 - **`true`**: Opts the segment into validation at whatever level is configured globally (see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults)). With the framework defaults, validation runs in development only and surfaces errors in the dev overlay. 47 - **`false`**: Opts the segment out (see [Disabling instant](#disabling-instant)). 48 - An **object**: Opts in with additional options. See [`level`](#level). 49 50 ### `level` 51 52 Sets the severity at which validation runs for this segment. 53 54 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 55 export const instant = { 56 level: 'warning', 57 } 58 ``` 59 60 - **`'warning'`**: Validates in development only. Errors appear in the dev overlay; the build is unaffected. 61 62 In the future a validation level that supports validation during build will be supported. Unless you are enabling experimental validation modes there is no need to specify level since the only level available is `"warning"`. 63 64 When `level` is omitted (or `instant = true` is used), the segment is validated at whatever level is configured globally — see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults). 65 66 ### Disabling instant 67 68 Set `false` on a layout or page to indicate that this segment is allowed to block when navigating to it. 69 70 This is useful when a deeper page should be instant but an ancestor can't be. For instance, if a shared layout cannot load instantly but you still want to assert that pages beneath this layout can be navigated to instantly, you can ensure that the pages have `instant = true` while the shared layout has `instant = false`. 71 72 ```tsx filename="app/tabs/layout.tsx" 73 export const instant = false 74 ``` 75 76 ```tsx filename="app/tabs/[tab]/page.tsx" 77 export const instant = true 78 ``` 79 80 Navigations from outside into a tab are allowed to block at the layout. Navigations between tabs are validated for instant UI. 81 82 You don't need to add `false` to ancestors of an instant page just because they do something blocking — a higher-up `instant = true` doesn't force its descendants to validate, and leaving an ancestor unconfigured is fine. Reach for `false` only when you've configured a deeper page as instant and need to exempt navigations that pass through a blocking ancestor. 83 84 ### Disabling static shell validation 85 86 Cache Components also validates that each page in your app produces a non-empty static shell at prerender time. To opt a route out of this validation, ensure the highest `instant` config in the route's tree is `false` — a `false` higher in the tree takes precedence over any deeper `true` for the static-shell check. 87 88 Setting `false` on the root layout disables static shell validation for the entire app. Place the `false` as low as possible — only as high as needed to cover the routes you want to opt out — so the rest of the app keeps validating. 89 90 ## How validation works 91 92 `instant` triggers validation at every shared layout boundary in the route. Validation runs during development (on page loads and HMR updates) and surfaces errors in the dev error overlay. 93 94 Each error identifies the component that would block navigation. The fix is usually to cache the data with `use cache` or wrap it in a `` boundary. 95 96 ## Configuring validation defaults 97 98 By default (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. The `experimental.instantInsights.validationLevel` config tunes this behavior — for example, to limit validation to segments that opt in explicitly via `instant`. 99 100 ```js filename="next.config.js" 101 module.exports = { 102 experimental: { 103 instantInsights: { 104 validationLevel: 'warning', 105 }, 106 }, 107 } 108 ``` 109 110 The supported levels are: 111 112 - **`'warning'`** _(framework default)_: Every Page and Default segment is implicitly validated at warning level (dev only). 113 - **`'manual-warning'`**: Only segments with an explicit `instant` are validated, at warning level (dev only). 114 115 Setting `instant = false` on a segment opts it out of validation entirely. 116 117 > **Good to know**: 118 > 119 > - The framework default may change in future versions to opt users into higher levels of validation. Because this feature is experimental, that change is not considered a breaking change. To pin a specific behavior, set `validationLevel` explicitly. 120 > - Framework-synthesized error routes (`/_global-error`, `/_not-found`) are excluded from implicit validation. To validate them, opt in explicitly with `instant`. 121 122 ## Inspecting loading states 123 124 The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled: 125 126 ```js filename="next.config.js" 127 module.exports = { 128 cacheComponents: true, 129 } 130 ``` 131 132 Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then turn on **Pause on navigations**. While the toggle is on: 133 134 - Refresh the page to freeze the initial static UI generated for the route, before any dynamic data streams in. 135 - Click a link to freeze the prefetched UI for the destination route. 136 137 When the UI is frozen, click **Resume** to let the current navigation finish. The toggle stays on, so the next refresh or link click pauses too. Turn it off when you are done. Use both page refreshes and link clicks to check that your loading states look right on first visit and on navigation. 138 139 ## Testing instant navigation 140 141 The `@next/playwright` package exports an `instant()` helper that holds back dynamic content while the callback runs against the instant UI. See the [guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for a full example. 142 143 ```typescript 144 import { instant } from '@next/playwright' 145 ``` 146 147 {/* TODO: remove when fixed and from prod-docs-release */} 148 149 ## Known issue: shared cookie across projects 150 151 The DevTools use a `next-instant-navigation-testing` cookie to hold back dynamic content and freeze the page at the instant UI. Because cookies are scoped to the domain and not the port, running multiple projects on the same domain (typically `localhost`) means the cookie is shared across them and can cause unexpected behavior. Clear the cookie or close the Navigation Inspector panel when switching between projects to avoid issues. 152 153 > **Good to know:** This will be fixed as part of stabilizing the feature. 154 155 ## TypeScript 156 157 ```tsx 158 type InstantConfig = 159 | true 160 | false 161 | { 162 level?: 'warning' 163 } 164 165 export const instant: InstantConfig = true 166 ``` 167 168 ## Version History 169 170 | Version | Changes | 171 | --------- | --------------------------------------------------- | 172 | `v16.x.x` | `instant` export introduced (Cache Components only) | 173

events.content: The product page awaits `getInventory()` (which calls `connection()`, forcing dynamic per-request rendering) before rendering anything — including the static title. That blocks the whole page, so nothing appears until the inventory fetch resolves. This project uses Cache Components / instant navigation (`cacheComponents: true` in `next.config.ts`), where the fix is to push the dynamic part behind its own `<Suspense>` boundary so the static shell (title) streams immediately.
